content: The recommended dosage of cefdinir for adults and adolescents is 600 mg per day. This can be administered as a single daily dose for 10 days, which has been shown to be as effective as twice-daily dosing. However, for pneumonia or skin infections, once-daily dosing has not been studied, so cefdinir capsules should be taken twice daily for these conditions. Cefdinir capsules can be taken with or without food. For adult patients with renal insufficiency, specifically those with a creatinine clearance (CLcr) of less than 30 mL/min, the recommended dose of cefdinir is 300 mg once daily. For males: CLcr = (weight in kg) × (140 – age in years) ÷ (72 × serum creatinine in mg/dL) For females: CLcr = 0.85 × the value calculated for males For pediatric patients, creatinine clearance can be estimated using the formula: CLcr = (K × body length or height in cm) ÷ serum creatinine in mg/dL, where K = 0.55 for children older than 1 year and 0.45 for infants up to 1 year. For pediatric patients with a creatinine clearance of less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m², the recommended dose of cefdinir is 7 mg/kg (up to a maximum of 300 mg) once daily. In patients undergoing chronic hemodialysis, cefdinir is removed from the body during dialysis. For these patients, the initial recommended dose is 300 mg or 7 mg/kg every other day. At the end of each hemodialysis session, an additional dose of 300 mg (or 7 mg/kg) should be administered. Subsequent doses of 300 mg (or 7 mg/kg) should then be given every other day.
